backlog.title: Distributed-PRD Include Dedup (Each File Imported At Most Once)
backlog.description: Rewrite the PRD §2.3 include-resolution model from a per-branch ancestry cycle check to a global flat dedup with elision. A given file is expanded at most once across the entire resolution; subsequent references are elided (dropped, or replaced by a non-resolvable marker comment). This guarantees the resolved document is a true fixed point: resolve(resolve(x)) === resolve(x), which is the property that ensures hash/snapshot/delta consistency (§4.1, §4.3). The change is localized to src/core/session-utils.ts and its tests.

milestones.title: Global Flat Dedup with Elision in expandIncludesRecursive
milestones.description: Rewrite the recursive include worker to use a single global shared visited set (passed by reference, not copied per branch), elide already-imported files instead of leaving their @tokens literal, and update all JSDoc to describe the new model. Then rewrite the existing tests that assert old per-branch semantics and add new invariant tests for dedup, elision, idempotency, and exponential-blowup protection.

tasks.title: Implement Global Flat Dedup + Elision + JSDoc Rewrite in expandIncludesRecursive
tasks.description: Rewrite the core algorithm in expandIncludesRecursive (src/core/session-utils.ts) so the visited set is global/shared/flat (mutated by reference, not copied per branch), and already-imported paths are elided rather than left literal. Rewrite all JSDoc on expandIncludesRecursive, resolvePRD, and resolveIncludes to describe the new dedup+elision model and cite §2.3. The current JSDoc actively endorses the old per-branch behavior and is factually wrong after this change.

subtasks.title: Rewrite expandIncludesRecursive: shared visited set + elision on second encounter
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/architecture/system_context.md for the full change-site map. The function expandIncludesRecursive is at ~line 448 of src/core/session-utils.ts (private, only called by resolvePRD at ~line 585). The current code copies the visited set per descent: `const childVisited = new Set(visited).add(abs)` and passes childVisited to the recursive call. The visited.has(abs) branch leaves the @token literal: `out += m[0]; continue;`. The stale-include warning condition is `replacement === undefined && token.endsWith('.md')` — elision is NOT undefined (it is a successful resolution that was already expanded on first encounter), so elision MUST NOT trigger the warning.
2. INPUT: The function signature is expandIncludesRecursive(content: string, baseDir: string, maxDepth: number, depth: number, visited: Set<string>, markers: boolean). The visited parameter arrives already seeded with the entry file's absolute path from resolvePRD (new Set<string>([absEntry])). No signature change is needed — the set is already passed by reference; only the MUTATION pattern changes.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD §2.3 global-flat-dedup. THREE changes within expandIncludesRecursive:
  (a) DEDUP, NOT ANCESTRY: Remove the `new Set(visited).add(abs)` copy. Instead, call `visited.add(abs)` BEFORE the recursive descent (mark visited before descending into the file, not after). Pass the SAME `visited` set (by reference) to the recursive call — do NOT create a new Set. This makes a diamond (A→C and B→C) resolve C exactly once; the second @C reference finds visited.has(abs) true.
  (b) ELIDE ON SECOND ENCOUNTER: In the `visited.has(abs)` branch, REPLACE the current `out += m[0]; continue;` (which leaves the @token literal) with ELISION: when markers is false, DROP the @token entirely (output nothing for it — do NOT echo m[0]). When markers is true, emit a STABLE REFERENCE COMMENT that names the path but contains NO resolvable @token of its own (e.g. `<!-- @include-ref: ${token} -->` — an HTML comment, which cannot match the RESOLVE_TOKEN regex on a re-scan because the path inside a comment is not preceded by @). The exact comment wording is an implementation detail; the contract is: names the path, contains no @token.
  (c) FIRST-ENCOUNTER ORDER: The existing loop already iterates matches in document order (matchAll preserves source order). The first textual occurrence of a path expands it inline (with optional markers around the expanded body, exactly as today via the existing `markers && replacement !== undefined` ternary). No change needed to the first-encounter path — it falls out naturally once the shared set replaces the copy.
  KEEP UNCHANGED: The `depth >= maxDepth` gate (defense-in-depth only now), the stat/isFile/ENOENT/error handling, the stale-include warning condition, and the marker format around EXPANDED bodies (`<!-- @include: ${token} -->` / `<!-- @end-include -->`).
  Also update the INLINE COMMENTS at the former `new Set(visited)` site (now `visited.add(abs)`) and at the `visited.has(abs)` branch to describe dedup + elision instead of ancestry + cycle-literal.
4. OUTPUT: The function returns Promise<string> — the content with includes recursively expanded inline, where each file appears at most once (first encounter expands, subsequent references elided). The output is consumed verbatim by resolvePRD → downstream callers (hashPRD, snapshotPRD, SessionManager, PRPPipeline, prd-selector). No interface change.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rewrite the JSDoc on expandIncludesRecursive in src/core/session-utils.ts. The current JSDoc says 'The visited set is PATH-BASED (per-branch ancestry)... diamond includes expand c in BOTH branches. A flat/global set would wrongly deduplicate diamonds.' This is now FACTUALLY WRONG — rewrite to describe global-flat-dedup + elision (shared set passed by reference, first-encounter wins, subsequent refs elided, elision emits no warning), citing PRD §2.3. Also update inline comments at the two change sites. This rides WITH the code work — do not create a separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Rewrite JSDoc on resolvePRD and resolveIncludes to match new dedup model
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/architecture/system_context.md. The JSDoc on resolvePRD (~line 540-568 of src/core/session-utils.ts) and resolveIncludes (~line 320-368) both reference the old per-branch model. resolvePRD's JSDoc says 'CYCLE DETECTION: a path-based visited Set... Diamond includes still expand c in both branches (the visited set is per-branch, not flat).' resolveIncludes' JSDoc references S1/S2/S3 staging and mentions cycle detection as an S2 feature. The IDENTITY/JSDoc block also has an @remarks mentioning 'Idempotency of resolvePRD (S3)' which should be updated to reflect the new true-fixed-point guarantee.
2. INPUT: The code change from P1.M1.T1.S1 is complete — expandIncludesRecursive now uses global flat dedup with elision. This subtask updates the JSDoc on the TWO CALLER/PEER functions (resolvePRD and resolveIncludes) to accurately describe the new model. The JSDoc on expandIncludesRecursive itself was already updated in S1.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite the JSDoc @remarks blocks:
  (a) resolvePRD: Replace the 'CYCLE DETECTION' bullet describing per-branch behavior with a 'GLOBAL FLAT DEDUPLICATION' bullet describing: a single global visited set keyed on resolved absolute path, first encounter expands inline, subsequent references are elided (dropped or marker comment), entry file is seeded in visited so self-includes are elided. Replace/update the 'IDEMPOTENCY' bullet: the resolved document is now a TRUE FIXED POINT — resolve(resolve(x)) === resolve(x) — because dedup ensures every resolvable token is expanded or elided on the first pass. Cite PRD §2.3. The 'MAX DEPTH' bullet should note it is now defense-in-depth only (dedup bounds recursion). The 'MARKERS' bullet should add the marker-reference-comment behavior for elided refs. The 'STALE-INCLUDE WARNING' bullet is unchanged.
  (b) resolveIncludes: Update any references to the recursive resolver's cycle detection to instead reference global flat dedup. Clarify that resolveIncludes is the SINGLE-LEVEL entry point and is NOT dedup-aware (it does not recurse and does not maintain a visited set). Cross-reference resolvePRD/expandIncludesRecursive for the recursive dedup model.
  No code logic changes — JSDoc and inline comments only.
4. OUTPUT: All three functions (expandIncludesRecursive from S1, resolvePRD and resolveIncludes from this subtask) have JSDoc that accurately describes the global-flat-dedup + elision model and cites §2.3. No interface change.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] This IS the documentation work — rewriting JSDoc on resolvePRD and resolveIncludes in src/core/session-utils.ts to match the new dedup+elision model from S1.

tasks.title: Rewrite Tests for New Dedup / Elision / Idempotency Semantics
tasks.description: The existing tests assert the OLD per-branch semantics (diamond expands shared file in both branches; cycle back-edge stays literal). They must be rewritten to assert the NEW contract: global flat dedup (each file once), elision on second encounter (dropped or marker comment), and idempotency as a true fixed point. New invariant tests must be added: diamond dedup, marker-mode reference comment, no-marker elision, idempotency fixed point, exponential-blowup guard, entry-is-its-own-cycle, and resolveIncludes single-level contract confirmation.

subtasks.title: Rewrite existing diamond/cycle tests to assert dedup + elision
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/architecture/test-impact-analysis.md for a complete table of affected tests. Five tests in tests/unit/core/prd-resolve.test.ts assert OLD behavior and must be rewritten. One test in tests/unit/core/prd-markers.test.ts ('no warn for a cycle back-edge') has an output assertion that changes. All tests use REAL tmpdir fixtures (mkdtempSync), NOT vi.mock — this strategy MUST be preserved.
2. INPUT: The new dedup+elision behavior is implemented in expandIncludesRecursive (from P1.M1.T1.S1). The five affected prd-resolve.test.ts tests and their exact current assertions are:
  - Test 1 'expands a diamond in both branches': FIXTURE shared.md='S', a.md='[@shared.md]', b.md='{@shared.md}', main.md='@a.md\n@b.md'. OLD assertion: out==='[S]\n{S}'. NEW: shared expands ONCE (first encounter via a.md), second @shared.md in b.md is ELIDED → out==='[S]\n{}'.
  - Test 2 'terminates a self-cycle leaving the back-edge literal': FIXTURE a.md='X @a.md Y', main.md='@a.md'. OLD: out==='X @a.md Y'. NEW: a expands; inner @a.md ELIDED → out==='X  Y'.
  - Test 3 'terminates a mutual cycle leaving the back-edge literal': FIXTURE a.md='A-TOP @b.md A-BOT', b.md='B-OPEN @a.md B-CLOSE', main.md='@a.md'. OLD: out==='A-TOP B-OPEN @a.md B-CLOSE A-BOT'. NEW: b's @a.md ELIDED → out==='A-TOP B-OPEN  B-CLOSE A-BOT'.
  - Test 4 'detects an include pointing back at the entry as a cycle': FIXTURE a.md='A @main.md END', main.md='@a.md'. OLD: out==='A @main.md END'. NEW: @main.md ELIDED → out==='A  END'.
  - Test 5 'recursively expands a nested chain (entry→a→b→c)': FIXTURE c.md='C', b.md='B(@c.md)', a.md='A(@c.md via b:@b.md)', main.md='start @a.md end'. OLD: out==='start A(C via b:B(C)) end' (c.md expands twice). NEW: c.md='C' expands once (first encounter in a.md's @c.md), b.md's @c.md ELIDED → out==='start A(C via b:B()) end'.
  Also from prd-markers.test.ts: Test 'no warn for a cycle back-edge' calls resolvePRD(a.md) where a.md='X @a.md Y'. Output changes from 'X @a.md Y' to 'X  Y'. The console.warn-NOT-called assertion REMAINS VALID (elision is silent). Only the output check needs updating.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite each of the five prd-resolve.test.ts tests to assert the NEW dedup+elision behavior. Rename describe/it titles to name the §2.3 invariant they lock in (e.g. 'deduplicates a diamond dependency — shared file expanded exactly once' instead of 'expands a diamond in both branches'). Update the prd-markers.test.ts cycle test's output assertion. The mock strategy (real tmpdir) is UNCHANGED — only fixture expectations change. For the mutual-cycle test (Test 3), also verify the `not.toContain('A-TOP A-TOP')` invariant still holds (it does — a is only expanded once).
4. OUTPUT: All existing tests in prd-resolve.test.ts and prd-markers.test.ts pass against the new implementation, asserting dedup + elision instead of per-branch expansion. Tests that were unaffected (single-level, base invariant, maxDepth, ENOENT, errors) remain unchanged.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Test descriptions / describe blocks should name the §2.3 invariant they lock in (dedup / elision / idempotency), so a future reader understands why each test exists. This rides WITH the test work.

subtasks.title: Add new invariant tests: idempotency fixed point, exponential-blowup guard, marker reference comment, diamond dedup
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/architecture/test-impact-analysis.md for the full list of required new tests (table N1-N7). All tests use REAL tmpdir fixtures (mkdtempSync). New tests should be added to tests/unit/core/prd-resolve.test.ts (dedup/idempotency/blowup tests) and tests/unit/core/prd-markers.test.ts (marker reference comment test). The describe blocks should name the §2.3 invariant being locked in.
2. INPUT: The new dedup+elision implementation from P1.M1.T1.S1 is complete and the existing tests have been rewritten (P1.M1.T2.S1). These new tests exercise invariants that did not exist under the old model and therefore have no predecessor tests to modify.
3. LOGIC: Add the following NEW test cases (PRD Requirement 2):
  (a) DIAMOND DEDUP (N1): Fixture A→B→D, A→C→D (4 files + entry E). E includes A; A includes B and C; B includes D; C includes D. Assert D's body appears EXACTLY ONCE in the resolved output (in its first-encounter position, which is under B's branch since B appears before C in A's text). Assert the second @D reference (from C) is ELIDED — no @D survivor in the output.
  (b) MARKER-MODE REFERENCE COMMENT (N2): Same diamond fixture but with markers:true. Assert the elided second @D reference is replaced by a STABLE REFERENCE COMMENT that (1) is present in the output, (2) contains NO resolvable @token, and (3) a second resolution pass over the marker-on output is BYTE-IDENTICAL (the comment does not trigger re-expansion — proves it is self-protecting).
  (c) NO-MARKER ELISION (N3): Same diamond with markers off (default). Assert the elided @D reference is simply ABSENT (the @token dropped). Assert no @D token survives in the output.
  (d) IDEMPOTENCY FIXED POINT (N4): A diamond-heavy fixture (files that mutually @-reference). Assert resolve(resolve(x)) === resolve(x) — call resolvePRD once, then call resolvePRD again on the result (writing it to a temp file first since resolvePRD takes a path), and assert byte-identical output. This is the headline invariant.
  (e) EXPONENTIAL-BLOWUP GUARD (N5): Create N (e.g. 8-10) mutually @-referencing files. Before this change, such a fixture would expand exponentially with depth until string overflow. Assert the resolved output size is LINEAR in the sum of file sizes (e.g. assert output length < some reasonable bound proportional to N * avg_file_size, not exponential). This is a regression test locking in the fix.
  (f) ENTRY-IS-ITS-OWN-CYCLE (N6): Entry file includes itself directly (@main.md inside main.md). Assert the self-include is ELIDED (the entry is seeded in visited). Assert no infinite loop, no @main.md survivor (no markers), no warning.
  (g) RESOLVEINCLUDES SINGLE-LEVEL (N7): Verify the single-level entry point's contract. A direct DUPLICATE @token within one entry file (e.g. main.md has @a.md twice) — confirm what happens (both expand inline, since resolveIncludes has no visited set). Document the behavior in the describe block. Per PRD: 'single-level dedup across siblings is out of the diamond problem; match whatever the shared lower-level scan does.' If resolveIncludes is now a thin/unused shim, note it; do not expand scope.
4. OUTPUT: Seven new test cases (across prd-resolve.test.ts and prd-markers.test.ts) that lock in the §2.3 dedup / elision / idempotency / blowup-protection invariants. All pass against the new implementation.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Test describe/it titles name the §2.3 invariant each test locks in (dedup / elision / idempotency / blowup-guard), so a future reader understands why each test exists. This rides WITH the test work.
